summary.intent: Assess the Callisto release tooling for unnecessary complexity, then act on the findings: slim the workflow policy checker, plan moving recovery into Callisto as `release --recover`, split ecosystem code per ecosystem, and verify overlap in derivation code.
summary.outcome: Slimmed the workflow policy checker from 633 to 175 lines (passes on the real workflow and rejects two deliberately broken copies), removed its self-test invocation from the justfile, fixed a stale ADR 13 mention, and opened a PR stacked on the tap PR. The recovery design, registry split and derive/release_decision overlap check were started or agreed but not completed in this transcript.

repo: Core design: the committed decision is the release authority, with no journal. Reruns observe real provider state (observed, adopted, performed or confirmed per operation). A fault-injection simulator drives the real executor through crash and provider outcomes.

The label-based recovery queue (#383) keeps a second record of release state in PR labels plus shell scripts and a dispatch chain. It contradicts the no-journal principle, can wedge later releases, and exists only in Callisto's own workflow, not in generated consumer workflows (ADR 13).

ADR README bar: an ADR records an architecturally significant decision with a credible rejected alternative. Behavior belongs in the spec and coding rules in AGENTS.md. ADR 13 (workflow mechanism) shouldn't be an ADR, and ADR 12 is still Proposed and overdue for a decision.
ADR 3's guardrail says not to add recovery commands without a new ADR. The plan is to treat `release --recover` as an amendment to ADR 3 instead.
Spec has about 250 criteria across five JSON files, duplicated across architecture doc, guide and 13 ADRs. The spec rule lives in AGENTS.md, so retiring it is the user's decision.

Workflow policy checker (.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh) now keeps rules that prevent a wrong publish or credential leak (secrets only in `execute`, no environment gate, pinned actions, per-job permissions) plus config-consistency checks.
registry.rs (1,233 lines) and registry_argv.rs (1,201 lines) mix Cargo, npm and PyPI logic; they can be split per ecosystem behind the existing trait, which also eases pending NuGet support.

code.finding: Rewritten from 633 lines with 28 self-test cases to 175 lines. It still passes on the real workflow and rejects deliberately broken copies; the justfile no longer invokes the self-test.

workflow: Measuring size and rule inventory before proposing cuts keeps the slimming grounded in what each check protects.
Switching branches under an open file invalidated a pending Write; re-reading the file before writing again fixed it.
Read-only investigations can run in a background agent while implementation work proceeds.
ADR test: if a change can be undone in one PR without anyone noticing, it isn't an ADR.

friction: The first Write of the slimmed policy script was refused because the file changed when switching branches, so it had to be re-read and rewritten.
Some Bash steps for shipping the PR were run twice (combined, then split), suggesting the first combined attempts failed or were redone.
open_items: Write a one-page design for `callisto release --recover` (find unfinished decision commits on main, skip fully observed ones, release the oldest) and have the action trigger it when needed.
Disable the label recovery queue in the meantime, keeping manual dispatch with a SHA, then delete the queue's shell scripts and tests and retire ADR 13 in the same PR.
Split registry.rs and registry_argv.rs per ecosystem behind the existing trait.
Review the background check of overlap between derive.rs (2,235 lines) and release_decision.rs (1,771 lines); it was unverified at this point.
Decide on ADR 12 (accept, split or drop).
Decide whether to retire the per-criterion spec files to cut documentation duplication.
